objectives.text: The program requirements contained in subpart B of 31 CFR Part 1010 apply to all financial institutions as defined in 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) or (c)(1), unless otherwise indicated, with institution-specific chapters providing additional program requirements.

citations.quote: Unless otherwise indicated, the program requirements contained in this subpart B apply to all financial institutions (as defined in 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) or (c)(1)).

objectives.text: To require covered financial institutions to maintain risk-based due diligence programs for correspondent accounts (for foreign financial institutions) and for private banking accounts that are reasonably designed to detect and report known or suspected money laundering activity, and to prohibit correspondent account relationships with foreign shell banks.

citations.quote: shall establish a due diligence program that includes appropriate, specific, risk-based, and, where necessary, enhanced policies, procedures, and controls that are reasonably designed to enable the covered financial institution to detect and report, on an ongoing basis, any known or suspected money laundering activity
A covered financial institution shall not establish, maintain, administer, or manage a correspondent account in the United States for, or on behalf of, a foreign shell bank.

obligations.actor: Each financial institution (as defined in 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) or (c)(1))
obligations.action: refer to subpart B of its chapter X Part for any additional program requirements

citations.quote: Each financial institution (as defined in 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) or (c)(1)) should refer to subpart B of its chapter X Part for any additional program requirements.

obligations.action: establish a due diligence program with appropriate, specific, risk-based, and, where necessary, enhanced policies, procedures, and controls reasonably designed to detect and report, on an ongoing basis, known or suspected money laundering activity conducted through or involving a correspondent account
obligations.trigger: the covered financial institution establishes, maintains, administers, or manages a correspondent account in the United States for a foreign financial institution

citations.quote: shall establish a due diligence program that includes appropriate, specific, risk-based, and, where necessary, enhanced policies, procedures, and controls that are reasonably designed to enable the covered financial institution to detect and report, on an ongoing basis, any known or suspected money laundering activity

obligations.action: maintain a due diligence program with policies, procedures, and controls reasonably designed to detect and report known or suspected money laundering or suspicious activity conducted through or involving a private banking account
obligations.trigger: the covered financial institution establishes, maintains, administers, or manages a private banking account in the United States

citations.quote: A covered financial institution shall maintain a due diligence program that includes policies, procedures, and controls that are reasonably designed to detect and report any known or suspected money laundering or suspicious activity conducted through or involving any private banking account

obligations.action: establish, maintain, administer, or manage a correspondent account in the United States for, or on behalf of, a foreign shell bank

citations.quote: A covered financial institution shall not establish, maintain, administer, or manage a correspondent account in the United States for, or on behalf of, a foreign shell bank.

obligations.action: take reasonable steps to ensure that a correspondent account it maintains for a foreign bank is not being used by that foreign bank to indirectly provide banking services to a foreign shell bank
obligations.trigger: the covered financial institution establishes, maintains, administers, or manages a correspondent account in the United States for a foreign bank

citations.quote: A covered financial institution shall take reasonable steps to ensure that any correspondent account established, maintained, administered, or managed by that covered financial institution in the United States for a foreign bank is not being used by that foreign bank to indirectly provide banking services to a foreign shell bank.

interactions.description: Section 1010.200 directs each financial institution to consult the subpart B program-requirement provisions located in its own chapter X Part (i.e., the institution-type-specific general provisions subparts), in addition to the general provisions of Part 1010.

citations.quote: should refer to subpart B of its chapter X Part for any additional program requirements

interactions.description: Section 1010.230(a) requires that beneficial-ownership identification/verification procedures for legal entity customers be included within the covered financial institution's anti-money laundering compliance program required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) and its implementing regulations; this CDD operational duty is treated as coordination-layer content under the ratified scope, but the cross-reference to the statutory program requirement is recorded here.

citations.quote: Covered financial institutions are required to establish and maintain written procedures that are reasonably designed to identify and verify beneficial owners of legal entity customers and to include such procedures in their anti-money laundering compliance program required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) and its implementing regulations.

notes: Per the ratified scope, this item's SAR/CTR/CDD operational-duty sections are treated as coordination layer and excluded from the obligations table: §1010.311 (CTR filing), §1010.312 (identification for currency-transaction reports), §1010.314 (anti-structuring prohibition, which is also adjacent to the fraud/enforcement boundary regime), §1010.410(e) (nonbank recordkeeping for fund transmittals), §1010.520(b)(3) (information-sharing record-search duty), and §1010.230 (beneficial ownership/CDD procedures) are noted only via cross-reference (interactions) rather than extracted as core obligations, since they are operational/coordination-layer duties rather than program-establishment ('pillars') obligations. §1010.630's shell-bank prohibition and indirect-use due-diligence duty were retained as in-scope obligations because the text binds them directly to the §1010.610 correspondent-account due-diligence-program framework; the working group should confirm whether a prohibition (as opposed to a program-establishment duty) properly belongs within the ratified 'program/pillars' scope, as this is extracted as written without resolving the ambiguity per the fidelity rule. The terms 'covered financial institution,' 'correspondent account,' 'private banking account,' 'foreign shell bank,' 'foreign financial institution,' and 'money laundering' are used in §1010.610/.620/.630 without definition in the excerpted text and are recorded as undefined-here. 'Financial institution' is defined in this excerpt only by cross-reference to 31 U.S.C. 5312(a)(2) or (c)(1), not restated in full.
